title: Directory enumeration failures silently produce a valid partial inventory
reasoning: An OSError from os.scandir terminates traversal of that directory without recording an invalid code. Consequently, an unreadable source subtree disappears from the inventory while is_valid can remain true. Scoring can then use incomplete production evidence, including omitting unsupported-language files.
reproduction: Inventory a readable root containing a readable Python file and a subdirectory whose enumeration raises PermissionError. The returned inventory contains only the readable file and reports no enumeration error.
recommendation: Propagate enumeration failures or emit an explicit invalid-entry signal that build_inventory converts to score_evidence_invalid.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file exercises general metrics aggregation and language registration, not scoring inventory traversal or filesystem failures.
suggestedRegressionTest: Exercise enumeration failures at both the root and a nested directory and assert that neither can yield a valid partial inventory.
minimumFixScope: src/slop_code/metrics/scoring/inventory.py traversal error propagation and focused inventory tests.

history.reasoning: The evidence file still exists, but the cited lines have changed. inventory.py:169–174 now raises InventoryEnumerationError on scandir failures; build_inventory at lines 222–229 catches it and returns no files with score_evidence_invalid. Read-only runtime validation injecting PermissionError at both root and nested directories passed, confirming is_valid=False and no partial inventory. Existing regression coverage checks both cases. No linked patch attempts were supplied. CodeGraph was unavailable; direct file inspection was used. An initial heredoc was blocked by filesystem restrictions; the same validation succeeded using python -c.
commands: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -B -c '<inject PermissionError into os.scandir at root and nested directories; assert empty files, score_evidence_invalid, and is_valid=False>'
